name: Question 5
problem:
Consider the homogeneous system ${x}^{′}(t)=Ax(t),$ where $A$ is a constant square matrix. You're given that the standard fundamental matrix ${Φ}_{0}(t)$ is the unique solution to the initial value problem

$$
{Φ}_{0}^{′}(t)=A{Φ}_{0}(t),\,{Φ}_{0}(0)={I}_{n}.
$$

A derivation of the formula for the solution $x(t)$ passing through $x(0)$ is presented below. 

$\text{L1}:\,$ Let ${Φ}_{0}(t)={e}^{At}$

$\text{L2}:\,$ $x(t)={Φ}_{0}(t)\,c$ for some constant vector $c$

$\text{L3}:\,$ $x(0)={Φ}_{0}(0)\,c$

$\text{L4}:\,$ ${Φ}_{0}(0)={I}_{n}$

$\text{L5}:\,$ $x(0)=c$

$\text{L6}:\,$ $x(t)={e}^{At}\,x(0)$

Select the correct options to justify each step of the reasoning.

$\,$ Line $\text{L2}$ follows from $\text{L1}$ by the
{{field-1}}.

$\,$ Line $\text{L4}$ follows from the definition of ${Φ}_{0}(t)$ as the standard fundamental matrix by
{{field-2}}.

$\,$ Line $\text{L6}$ follows from line $\text{L2}$ by substitution from lines {{field-3}}.
worked_solution:
Let's justify each of the selected steps.

- We first consider lines $\text{L1}$ and $\text{L2}.$ Since ${Φ}_{0}(t)={e}^{At}$ is a fundamental matrix for the system, every solution of the system can be written as 

$$
x(t)={Φ}_{0}(t)\,c\,\text{for some constant vector }c.
$$

Thus, $\text{L2}$ follows from $\text{L1}$ by the $\text{properties of a fundamental matrix}.$

- Next, we consider line $\text{L4}.$ By definition, the standard fundamental matrix ${Φ}_{0}(t)$ satisfies the initial value problem

$$
{Φ}_{0}^{′}(t)=A{Φ}_{0}(t),\,{Φ}_{0}(0)={I}_{n}.
$$

The second condition here is exactly line $\text{L4},$ so $\text{L4}$ follows from the definition of ${Φ}_{0}(t)$ as the standard fundamental matrix by $\text{using the initial condition }{Φ}_{0}(0)={I}_{n}.$

- Finally, we consider lines $\text{L2}$ and $\text{L6}.$ Substituting ${Φ}_{0}(t)={e}^{At}$ from $\text{L1}$ and $c=x(0)$ from $\text{L5}$ into $x(t)={Φ}_{0}(t)\,c,$ we obtain

$$
x(t)={e}^{At}\,x(0).
$$

Thus, $\text{L6}$ follows from $\text{L2}$ and substitution from $\text{L1}\text{ and }\text{L5}.$

EXPLANATION

Let's justify each of the selected steps.

  • We first consider lines L1 and L2. Since Φ0(t)=eAt is a fundamental matrix for the system, every solution of the system can be written as x(t)=Φ0(t)cfor some constant vector c. Thus, L2 follows from L1 by the properties of a fundamental matrix.

  • Next, we consider line L4. By definition, the standard fundamental matrix Φ0(t) satisfies the initial value problem Φ0′(t)=AΦ0(t),Φ0(0)=In.
